thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired - PD#INC-8972 - gpu-node-03 (us-west-2) unreachable; symptom: kubelet NotReady + host not responding to SSH.

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to leo-oncall (1st) and escalation to oncall-sre.

leo-oncall: Acked. I'm on it. Pinging oncall channel and grabbing console.

raj: I saw metrics spike for model-serving-queue in us-west-2 ~ 02:12 UTC. Some inference 5xxs reported. Reproducing now.

priya: Confirming: error rate for hosted-api route /v1/generate jumped to ~6% (p95 latency also up). Likely impacted customers on dedicated clusters too.

leo-oncall: Quick triage steps: 1) check node status 2) check kubelet/journal 3) check BMC/IPMI 4) cordon + failover. I'll run `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl describe node gpu-node-03`.

alice: I'm pulling logs from the autoscaler and routing layer to see if traffic was drained.

leo-oncall: Node shows `NotReady` and `kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing` entries in the last boot cycle per node logs we can access. SSH times out. Looks like hardware/kernel panic.

devops-bot: Alert: remote-console-session opened to bmc-gpu-node-03 at 02:18 UTC. Firmware reports no OS heartbeat.

raj: Can we failover pods? If kubelet dead, controller should reschedule, but GPU pods are stateful/long-running; we should cordon & drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to force reschedule to other hosts. Note potential local cache loss for KV prefix caching.

leo-oncall: Cordon/Drain in progress: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-03` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`. Posting output: 
```
node/gpu-node-03 cordoned
evicting pod serving/model-a-7c9df...: eviction failed - pod has local storage
force deleting pod serving/model-a-7c9df... (grace period 30s)
```

priya: Traffic routing: I've enabled model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive routes to use model-a-quantized in us-west-2 while we recover. This should reduce 5xxs.

tom-support: Noting customer impact: two customers on Dedicated had degraded throughput; escalated to CS and emailed kids-platform team.

leo-oncall: Attempting soft-reboot via BMC (IPMI reset) now. If that fails, request rack tech to power cycle.

devops-bot: BMC reset returned `watchdog timed out` then `rebooting`. Will monitor console.

maria-oncall: Jumping in for handoff — will be on-call for the next hour. @leo-oncall can you summarise current blockers?

leo-oncall: Summary for handoff: root cause likely kernel panic on gpu-node-03. Node unresponsive to SSH. Kubelet NotReady. Drain forced; most serving pods moved to other nodes but a handful forced-deleted and restarted (possible cache warmup). Failover routing and model fallback applied. Reboot via BMC initiated; awaiting node to come back. Customer impact: ~5% errors for 12 minutes, targeted dedicated customers saw reduced throughput, mitigation in place. Logs/commands run: 
```
kubectl get nodes
kubectl describe node gpu-node-03
journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -i panic
ipmitool -H bmc-gpu-node-03 -U admin -P *** chassis power reset
kubectl drain gpu-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria-oncall: Thanks — I'll watch the console and handle followups. If node fails to boot within 10 minutes escalate to rack tech for physical RMA. Also schedule a follow-up postmortem and include kernel logs and firmware revision.

raj: I'll capture kernel oops and upload to the incident folder. Also double-check if the node had any recent kernel updates or driver rollouts last night.

alice: Observability note: adding annotation to the incident and creating a dashboard showing p95/p99 and error rate for affected routes for the last 60m.

leo-oncall: Node is showing POST messages on console now, seems to be rebooting cleanly. Fingers crossed.

devops-bot: New log: kubelet registered gpu-node-03 at 02:36 UTC; status Ready.

priya: Confirming: pod distribution looks healthy, autoscaler rebalanced GPU load. Error rate dropping back to baseline.

tom-support: Notifying customers that the cluster recovered and we mitigated with fallbacks; CS sent follow-up notes.

maria-oncall: I'll keep monitoring for 30 minutes then close the pager. Please add any action items.

raj: Action items: (1) collect full kernel crashdump + upload (2) run hardware diagnostics on GPU and NIC (3) check firmware/kernel/drivers for mismatch (4) propose automation to cordon nodes with repeated kernel Oops before serving traffic.

leo-oncall: :white_check_mark: Agreed. Adding those to incident doc and assigning. Great team, nice rapid mitigation.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-8972 acknowledged by leo-oncall and closed after recovery (duration ~24m).
